subject_class: organisations that invite third parties to report problems with their AI systems and products

disclosure_bar.rule: presence of at least 3 of 5 link classes

patterns.reporting_channel: report a|submit a|contact us|get in touch|report an issue|feedback|report concern
patterns.response_commitment: response time|within \d+ (business )?days|service level|sla|acknowledg|we aim to respond

frame.population_description: the 123 distinct subjects in the union of company-practice.discovery-v1.json, lab-practice.discovery.json, regulator-transparency.discovery.json
frame.inclusion_rule: Every candidate in the frozen union was attempted exactly once at run time; no candidate was added, dropped, substituted or re-ordered. The grid digest is published, so the population is checkable.

score_caveat: The headline bar was fixed before scoring and is the estate's declared 3-of-5 rule. A score of exactly 0 or 1 is refused by the estate G2 rule; where that happens the class census is the statistic, not the score.
limitations: A link-class presence check records observable strings in public bytes at observed_at. Absence on the landed URL is not evidence of absence elsewhere.
This measures disclosure presence, not disclosure quality, truth, or compliance.
A refusal is recorded in its own state and is never converted to a zero or a failure.
The frame is a curated union of the estate's own frozen populations; it is not a probability sample of all AI organisations.
